sections.h2: Which office files a Missouri deed?
sections.html:
The county recorder where the parcel lies. Section 442.380 requires any written instrument that conveys real estate, or touches it in law or equity, to be filed in that county's recorder office after it has been acknowledged or proved and certified.

Titles differ across Missouri. Moniteau County lets the circuit clerk act as recorder, so the office sits in Room 102 of the courthouse at 200 E. Main Street in California, and the Missouri Association of Counties lists 573-796-2071 for it. Other counties run a stand-alone recorder of deeds. Phone the county that holds your parcel before mailing a thing.

Filing is not what makes a deed binding between the people who signed it. Section 442.400 withholds validity from an unrecorded instrument as to everyone except the parties and those with actual notice. A buyer who never files therefore leaves the purchase open to anyone who had no actual notice of it.

sections.h2: What must a Missouri deed contain before the recorder will accept it?
sections.html:
It needs the grantor's signature, a proper acknowledgment, a legal description, and a mailing address for at least one grantee. Those four items come from three different statutes, so sellers often miss one.

  • Signature. Section 442.130 says the person granting the land signs, or a lawful agent signs for them.
  • Marital status. The same section requires any written instrument conveying real estate to say whether each individual grantor, mortgagor or other signer is married or unmarried.
  • Acknowledgment. The signature has to be acknowledged or proved before an authorized officer. Within the state, section 442.150 names a sealed court, its judge, justice or clerk, and notaries public. A notary in another state can take it as well.
  • Legal description and grantee address. Section 59.330 requires a legal description of the land, plus a mailing address for one grantee on every deed except easements and rights of way. A recorder is told not to file a deed missing either one, yet the statute says the instrument's validity and its constructive notice survive the omission.

The acknowledgment certificate has its own wording rules. Section 442.210 sets out sample certificates for individuals, for people signing through an attorney in fact, and for corporations, and the notary adds a signature and title at the end.

sections.h2: How should the pages be formatted for a Missouri recorder?
sections.html:
A recorder may turn away a deed over margins alone. The requirements appear in subsection 1 of section 59.310, and a title company usually handles them, but a seller preparing a quitclaim or family deed on their own should check each one.

  • Single-sided pages that are loose, not bound, with nothing stapled on unless a statute demands the attachment.
  • Print of eight points or larger, in black or dark ink, on white or light-colored paper weighing 20 pounds or more.
  • A three inch blank band across the top of page one, held for the recorder's stamp, and margins of 0.75 inch on every other edge.
  • Dark-ink signatures, each with the signer's name typed, printed or stamped underneath.

The first page, below that three inch margin, must show the document title, its date, every grantor's name and marital status, every grantee's name, any statutory addresses, the legal description, and the book and page of any referenced record. A deed that misses the format can still go on record, with a $25 surcharge. Several kinds of paper skip the format rules entirely: anything signed before 2002, military separation papers, documents executed overseas, certified copies, instruments where an original party has died or become incapacitated, and court judgments. When the recorder rejects a document, it must be returned with the reason.

sections.h2: What will the recorder charge on a Missouri deed?
sections.html:
Plan on $5 for page one and $3 for every page that follows, for any deed or instrument other than a plat or survey. A three page warranty deed therefore runs $11, before any surcharge the situation triggers.

Charges a Missouri recorder may collect under RSMo 59.310
ServiceFee
Recording a deed or other instrument$5 for page one, then $3 per page
Copy of a recorded instrumentNo more than $2 for page one, $1 per page after
Certificate and seal apart from a recording$1
Release or assignment of several items$5 for each item past the first
Subdivision or condominium plat$25 a sheet
Survey of one or more tracts$5 a sheet
Document that fails the format rules$25 added

The recorder may also set a reasonable charge for other use of equipment, staff and facilities, and for duplicate records on media other than paper. Ask the office for the total on your pages before a check goes out.

sections.h2: Can you record a Missouri deed electronically?
sections.html:
Only where the county recorder has chosen to offer it. Section 59.563 lets the recorder of deeds in any county or municipality set up an electronic format for recording and filing, and it also says no recorder has to establish, accept or transmit documents electronically.

That leaves three practical routes for a seller or buyer. Your closing agent can submit it. You can carry the paper original to the counter yourself. Or you can mail it with a check for the page charges and a return address. Whichever way you choose, call the office first and ask how it wants the deed delivered and how to make out the check.

When the deed carries a signer who has died or become incapacitated, such as a deed signed years ago and never filed, the format exemption in section 59.310 applies. Ask the recorder how they want that kind of document presented.

sections.h2: Why does the filing step matter when you sell for cash?
sections.html:
Because the buyer's title rests on it. A cash purchaser in Missouri still expects a signed, acknowledged deed to be filed in the right county, and whoever handles closing will look at what is already on record against the property.

If the house reached you through a death, the route to clean title often passes through the recorder. A beneficiary deed works only if it was already on file when the owner died, and a small estate affidavit becomes evidence of ownership once a copy is filed with the recorder of each county where the real estate sits. Our guide to Missouri beneficiary deeds builds on the same filing rules.

Before listing, pull your current vesting deed and compare its names, marital status statements and legal description against what you plan to sign. If the record and your deed disagree, ask the recorder what correction document they accept.

faqs.q: What does a Missouri recorder charge for a deed?
faqs.a: Statute sets $5 for page one and $3 for each further page, with plats and surveys priced separately. A deed that fails the format rules costs $25 more. Call the office for the exact total.

faqs.q: Must a Missouri deed be notarized?
faqs.a: It must be acknowledged or proved and certified, and a notary public can do that inside Missouri, as can a sealed court or its judge, justice or clerk. Section 442.150 lists the officers.

faqs.q: Does an unrecorded Missouri deed still count?
faqs.a: It binds the two parties and anyone who actually knew of it. Section 442.400 denies it validity against everyone else until it is deposited with the recorder, so file it quickly.

faqs.q: Can a Missouri recorder turn my deed down?
faqs.a: Yes. A deed that breaks the format rules of section 59.310, or lacks a legal description or a grantee's mailing address under section 59.330, can be refused. The rejection comes back with a stated reason.

faqs.q: Do I state marital status on a Missouri deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 442.130 requires every written instrument conveying real estate to say whether each individual grantor, mortgagor or other signer is married or unmarried. Place it beside the name.
